prompts: Words are tied to each other, and nobody here can see how. {WS}/site is a saved copy of a Portuguese creative dictionary. Explore this universe of words: collect what the site knows and build {WS}/universe/index.html, a single file that sums the universe up in one view and lets someone search for a word and find how it relates to others. The best way to show it is your call, and that view is what we care about most. So people can share a word, opening the page with ?word=saudade must show that word and its relations. Save the data as {WS}/words.json, mapping each word to the words it is linked to, and record in {WS}/result.json: words (how many), relations (how many distinct pairs) and most_connected. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.

Verified data consistency, reciprocal links, unique-pair counts, JavaScript syntax, and direct-file rendering in Chromium—including the saudade view.

--- README.md ---
# Entre palavras

Open universe/index.html directly in a browser. No server, build, or data fetch is required. Add ?word=saudade to select a word. Search, click a node or a relation, highlight a theme, pan, zoom, or reset the view.

Found 250 canonical words and 743 distinct undirected relations. palavra and tempo tie for highest degree at 16. Only synonym and analogous-word sections count. Navigation is excluded, redirects resolved, URL escapes decoded, case normalized, and accents preserved. Seven unresolved links are excluded. All 250 word pages are included, even if not linked from the home page. Theme grouping comes from the source; distance does not encode semantic similarity.

words.json contains symmetric adjacency lists. result.json records counts and all tied leaders in most_connected. audit.json records extraction decisions and unresolved links. build.py reproduces extraction; assemble.py embeds the data in the HTML. verify.py checks adjacency symmetry, self-edge exclusion, counts, preserved accents, and agreement between embedded and exported data. JavaScript syntax was checked with Node; the file and the saudade URL were opened and visually checked in Chromium. The selected word has five neighbors: ansiedade, carinho, dor, esperança, nostalgia.

The HTML is self-contained except for optional Google Fonts; system-font fallbacks work offline. Screenshots in universe document the overview and shared word view.

from pathlib import Path
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from urllib.parse import unquote,urlsplit
import json,unicodedata,re,collections,math,random
root=Path('.')
def norm(s):return unicodedata.normalize('NFC',s.strip()).lower()
class Page(HTMLParser):

  super().__init__();self.h=False;self.t=False;self.section=None;self.word='';self.theme='';self.links=[];self.redirect=None;self.feed(s)
 def handle_starttag(self,tag,attrs):
  a=dict(attrs)
  if tag=='h1':self.h=True
  if tag=='p' and a.get('class')=='tema':self.t=True
  if tag=='section':self.section=a.get('id')
  if tag=='a' and self.section in ('sinonimos','analogas'):self.links.append(a.get('href',''))
  if tag=='meta' and a.get('http-equiv','').lower()=='refresh':self.redirect=re.split('url=',a.get('content',''),flags=re.I)[-1].strip()
 def handle_endtag(self,tag):
  if tag=='h1':self.h=False
  if tag=='p':self.t=False
  if tag=='section':self.section=None
 def handle_data(self,s):
  if self.h:self.word+=s
  if self.t:self.theme+=s
pages={norm(p.name):Page(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')) for p in (root/'site').glob('*.html')}
def resolve(href,seen=None):
 name=norm(unquote(urlsplit(href).path).split('/')[-1]);seen=set() if seen is None else seen

for name,p in pages.items():

  raw+=1;b=resolve(href)
  if b is None:missing.append({'source':a,'href':href})
  elif a!=b:words[a].add(b);words[b].add(a)
words={k:sorted(v) for k,v in sorted(words.items())};edges=sorted({tuple(sorted((a,b))) for a,bs in words.items() for b in bs});maxdegree=max(map(len,words.values()));leaders=[k for k,v in words.items() if len(v)==maxdegree]
result={'words':len(words),'relations':len(edges),'most_connected':leaders}
(root/'words.json').write_text(json.dumps(words,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2),encoding='utf-8');(root/'result.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2),encoding='utf-8')
names=list(words);groups=sorted(set(themes.values()));random.seed(17);nodes=[]
for i,w in enumerate(names):

# Deterministic repulsion makes every node inspectable while preserving thematic neighborhoods.
for iteration in range(160):

(root/'universe').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(root/'universe/data.tmp').write_text(json.dumps(data,ensure_ascii=False),encoding='utf-8')
